sections.h2: Where do I search property records in Pinellas County?
sections.html:
Start with the Official Records search run by the Pinellas County clerk and comptroller at mypinellasclerk.gov. The clerk's records page groups land records, deeds, mortgages, liens, judgments and plats in one place, separate from court case records.

The clerk's records liaison is at 315 Court Street, Room 400, Clearwater, FL 33756, with a phone line at (727) 464-3341. The Customer Information Center number printed on the fee schedule is (727) 464-7000. If a document is not free online, the clerk's copy request center gives a quote.

Ownership, parcel and value data live elsewhere, at the property appraiser. The appraiser's site at pcpao.gov offers quick, map and advanced search for real property and tangible personal property. Use both: the clerk shows what was recorded, and the appraiser shows how the parcel is valued and who is on the tax roll.

sections.h2: How big and how dense is Pinellas County?
sections.html:
The county is a peninsula 38 miles long and 15 miles wide at its widest point, with 280 square miles and 588 miles of coastline. The county's own fast facts page calls it the most densely populated county in Florida, at 3,425 residents on each square mile, and the second smallest by land area.

It became the state's 48th county on January 1, 1912, when voters chose to separate from Hillsborough County. Clearwater is the county seat, St. Petersburg is the largest of 24 municipalities, and Tarpon Springs was the first city incorporated, in 1887. The 2020 Census counted 959,107 residents, which ranks seventh in the state.

County materials name tourism, financial services, life science, manufacturing, defense, aviation and information technology as key sectors. The practical point for sellers is that the county contains 24 cities with separate codes. A parcel may be inside a city or in unincorporated land, and the deed and records work is the same either way because one clerk records for the whole county.

sections.h2: How many parcels and what kinds of property are in the county?
sections.html:
The property appraiser's home page lists 437,624 real property parcels, of which 408,947 are residential. That mix includes 241,442 single family units, 103,445 condo units, 22,112 townhome or PUD units, 44,323 manufactured home units and 101,180 multifamily rental units.

The same list shows 23,010 commercial parcels and 57,476 tangible personal property accounts. If your home is a condo or a manufactured home unit, ask the clerk which recorded documents apply to it.

sections.h2: Which fees apply when a Pinellas deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Recording fees follow state law, and the deed itself may carry stamp tax. The clerk posts a PDF at mypinellasclerk.gov/Home/Fee-Schedule that says its charges come from statute, county ordinance and administrative order.

Under section 28.24(13) of the Florida Statutes, page one of an instrument up to 14 by 8.5 inches costs $5.00 and each later page costs $4.00. Extra items include $1.00 per name past four, a modernization trust fund charge of $1.00 plus $0.50 per added page, and a technology charge of $4 per page.

Deed stamps in Pinellas are seventy cents for each $100 of consideration, the statewide rate outside Miami-Dade. Everyone on the deed is liable for it no matter who agrees to pay. Ask your closing agent for a written recording total ahead of the closing date.

  • Warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds are on the Department of Revenue's taxable list.
  • The department lists a deed from a personal representative acting under a probated will as not taxable.
  • Divorce deeds for the marital home are exempt.

sections.h2: What formalities does a Florida deed need?
sections.html:
Section 689.01 requires a written deed with two witnesses watching the signing, and audio-video witnessing is permitted. No seal is needed.

Other charges may share your closing statement. The clerk's schedule under section 28.24 prints $60.00 to process a tax deed application and $30.00 plus $15.00 per added page for plats. Mortgages carry 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured.

Recording protects the buyer against a later purchaser, so have the title company send the deed to the clerk on closing day and keep the stamped copy.

sections.h2: What else does the county say about itself that matters to a seller?
sections.html:
The fast facts page lists $56,737 as the median household income, more than 38,400 businesses and 492,537 people employed. It credits the county parks department with over 20,000 acres of parks and preserves, 117 miles of recreational trails and about 20 million park visits in 2021.

On transport, it reports 4,379 PSTA bus stops, 210 buses and 10.2 million riders a year, plus roughly 4,500 miles of paved roads. The highest natural point is 110 feet, near State Road 580 and Countryside Boulevard in Clearwater. The page also points to the Young Rainey STAR Center, a former weapons production site now used for research and manufacturing.

None of this replaces the parcel record, but it gives you talking points for a listing and context for a buyer who is new to the area.

sections.h2: Which recorded items should a Pinellas owner look for first?
sections.html:
Pull the chain of title and look for anything recorded against the property that the buyer's lender and closing agent will turn up. Typical finds include a mortgage never released, a contractor's lien, or a judgment filed under an owner's name.

  • Search the owner's name and the legal description, not only the street address.
  • Look for recorded mortgages without a matching satisfaction.
  • Look for liens, judgments and code enforcement filings.
  • Confirm the deed in your name was recorded and names every owner correctly.

A 2020 Department of Revenue advisement looked at a lady bird deed in which the life tenants kept full powers. It found no present beneficial interest passed and no stamp tax on those facts. Because that guidance covers one fact pattern, a title attorney should review yours.

Most transfers of title count as a change of ownership under Save Our Homes, with exceptions such as moves between spouses. A quitclaim to a relative can therefore lift the assessment to full value the following January.

faqs.q: Who is the recorder for Pinellas County?
faqs.a: The clerk and comptroller's office. It keeps deeds, mortgages, liens, judgments and plats, and its records page links to the search.

faqs.q: Can I search Pinellas County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Official Records search that the clerk's View Records page links to. Items not free online can be requested through the clerk's copy request center, which gives a cost quote.

faqs.q: How much is the documentary stamp tax on a Pinellas County deed?
faqs.a: Seventy cents on every $100 of price. Every county except Miami-Dade uses that rate, and the clerk takes it at recording.

faqs.q: What is the statutory recording fee in Pinellas County?
faqs.a: Section 28.24(13) sets $5.00 on page one and $4.00 on later pages, before the trust fund and technology charges. Check the clerk's PDF fee schedule for the current total.

faqs.q: Where do I find parcel and value information for Pinellas County?
faqs.a: Use the property appraiser at pcpao.gov, which offers address, owner, parcel ID and map search. The office lists four service locations and a main phone line of (727) 464-3207.
